sections.heading: Planning your The Bronze interior
sections.text:
In a boutique District 12 home, the interior is usually judged at close range. There is little space to hide a loose wardrobe, an unfinished kitchen or a cluttered entry, and the finish needs to be consistent from the door to the bedroom. That is a natural brief for Maison. We design built-in carpentry — an entry cabinet, a living-room joinery wall, a fitted kitchen, and full-height wardrobes, with a headboard wall in the main bedroom if the plan allows it — and we present the work the way a professional interior is photographed, including closer shots of stone, veneer, profiles and junctions, not only a wide corner-to-corner view. We do not use IKEA-style flat-pack furniture as the backbone of the home.

No official floor plan is on file, so typologies, room sizes and a sample layout are not published here, and we will not invent a typical The Bronze plan. The Orie, also in District 12 at Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, is a nearby page on this site; it is a much larger development and is not a typologies reference for this building. We will not invent walking times to Toa Payoh town, to Balestier, or to any MRT station. Check your own stack, facing and the management rules, which in a small building can be quite specific about access, working hours and protection of common areas.

When a key date is in writing, inspect defects, measure, and obtain renovation approval before fabrication. A moderate carpentry scope is often planned at about six to ten weeks on site after approvals; that is an editorial allowance, not a guarantee. WhatsApp Maison with your approved plan when you have it. We are not affiliated with the developer.
